primary_source_cited_by_CR1457: Gonzalez, H. M. and Patton, R. J., 'Development and Fabrication of 55-Inch Diameter Scale Model S-II Common Bulkheads', North American Rockwell Corp. Report No. SDL 468, May 1964 (CR-1457 ref 6-4, report p. 6-19; title as printed in the reference list)
what_could_read: full text of CR-1457 (404-page PDF, pdftotext plus page image of the figure). Only the digest in CR-1457 was read; the SDL 468 original was NOT found or opened. Individual test pressures and specimen dimensions are not tabulated in CR-1457.
shell: hemisphere (two data points); boundary conditions of the S-II scale-model tests: null (not stated in CR-1457). CR-1457 notes one further test point was discarded for a faulty edge condition and that three points were discarded for stresses too high for reliable plasticity reduction factors.

geometry.note: Radius not stated in CR-1457. The reference title says '55-Inch Diameter Scale Model', but which diameter that is (bulkhead base, tank) is not stated here. The figure abscissa is R_Max/rho (rho = shell-wall radius of gyration, about h/2 for equal facings); the two hemisphere points plot near R_Max/rho of about 240 (visual read from Fig. 6.2-3, approximate, not stated in text).

faces.note: not stated in CR-1457 for these tests. Section 6.2 elsewhere uses E_f, nu_e, t_f, h as symbols only.

core.type: honeycomb sandwich dome per the S-II program (type for these specific data not stated in the CR-1457 passage read)

predicted_pressure_and_basis: Classical small-deflection theory for a sandwich sphere WITH core transverse shear (Yao 1962 / Plantema 1966 solution, CR-1457 Eqs. 6.2-1 to 6.2-12, buckling coefficient Kc vs shear-crimping parameter Vc), times plasticity reduction factor eta where stresses were above the elastic range. Absolute predicted pressures not given.
measured_over_predicted_as_stated: Recommended design knock-down gamma_d = 0.20 for hemispheres (Eq. 6.2-13), 'based on' the two hemisphere data points. Plotted points (Fig. 6.2-3) read by eye at roughly 0.22 to 0.23 (my visual estimate of a triangle marker pair; NOT a number printed in the report).

locations.text_gamma_d_definition: report p. 6-8, Section 6.2.1.2 'Empirical Knock-Down Factor' (PDF p. ~354)
locations.figure: Figure 6.2-3, report p. 6-9 (PDF page 355); legend: hemispheres at room temperature (triangles), approximate ellipsoids (dots), ellipsoids with thermal gradient (boxed dots)
locations.recommendation: report p. 6-10 Eq. 6.2-13 and p. 6-12 (design rule: gamma_d = 0.20 hemispheres, 0.35 ellipsoids/torispherical when Vc < 2.0; gamma_d = 1.0 when Vc >= 2.0, the weak-core shear-crimping region described on p. 6-7. Inequality direction read from the p. 6-7 text because the p. 6-12 OCR is garbled)

quotes.text: the available test data from sandwich dome constructions are very scarce
two data points from hemispheres and six data points from domes
final designs must be substantiated by test

notes: Report says the S-II data are the ONLY useful dome data it uncovered. The knock-down is applied to classical theory that includes core shear, and the weak-core domain (Vc >= 2) is said to be imperfection-insensitive, so gamma_d = 0.20 / 0.35 applies to the stiff and moderately stiff core range (Vc < 2) and 1.0 to Vc >= 2 (p. 6-7 text; the p. 6-12 inequality symbols are garbled in OCR and were not checked against the page image). Section 6.2.1.1: a sandwich cylinder analogy from Yao/Plantema, assumptions R/t_c >> 1, equal facings, isotropic core shear. Two ellipsoid specimens carried a thermal gradient (inner face about +280 F, outer about +10 F) that was ignored in data reduction.

geometry.note: sphere radius not applicable; slant length not read.

core.type: aluminum honeycomb, 5052 perforated walls 0.0038 cm, 0.64 cm cells, ribbon meridional, one splice per panel; FM 123-2 adhesive, bond about 0.025 cm
core.G_c: Table IV lists 'honeycomb core' G = 0.097 GN/m2 (0.014e6 psi) and E = 0.262 GN/m2, modelled as isotropic with nu 0.35; a footnote says this is core plus adhesive total stiffness (4.90 MN/m). Whether it is the transverse shear modulus is not stated, so treat as a model input, not a measured transverse G_c.

measured.buckling_pressure_cone1_cone2_cone3: 38.13 / 30.27 / 21.24 kN/m2 = 5.53 / 4.39 / 3.08 psi, six circumferential waves each (Table III, report p. 16)
measured.buckling_definition: strain-rate reversal; taken 8.5 percent below the observed pressure plateau (plateaus 41.7 / 33.1 / 23.2 kN/m2 = 6.046 / 4.800 / 3.371 psi) (text p. 8)
measured.ultimate_failure_pressure: cone 1 45.51 kN/m2 (6.60 psi), cone 2 44.40 kN/m2 (6.44 psi), cone 3 27.30 kN/m2 (3.96 psi) (Fig. 12, Figs. 18-19 captions); cones carried 18 / 48 / 30 percent more load after buckling (text p. 9); failure violent

predicted_pressure_and_basis.SALORS: 50.06 / 37.99 / 26.20 kN/m2 (7.26 / 5.51 / 3.80 psi), n = 7 waves (shell-of-revolution FE, linear prebuckling stress, live pressure)
predicted_pressure_and_basis.BOSOR2: 53.78 / 39.85 / 27.79 kN/m2 (7.80 / 5.78 / 4.03 psi), n = 7 (nonlinear prebuckling stress, not live)
predicted_pressure_and_basis.both_include_core_shear: null (the model treats the sandwich wall as layered/orthotropic with the Table IV core stiffness; whether shear deformation was included is not confirmed from the text read)

measured_over_predicted_as_stated: report states required reductions to the prediction: BOSOR 2 about 29 percent (cone 1) and 24 percent (cones 2, 3); SALORS about 24, 20, 19 percent for cones 1, 2, 3 (text p. 9); compares with a 25 percent reduction recommended in NASA SP-8019 and 20 percent from an earlier magnesium cone test. A test/prediction ratio is not printed.

quotes.text: Three aluminum honeycomb sandwich conical shells with a 120 degree apex angle
Theoretical buckling predictions for shells are usually higher than actual test results.

notes: Closest measured honeycomb-sandwich external-pressure shell found with full numbers, but it is a cone with ring edge supports, so its knockdown is not a sphere or dome knockdown. Imperfection surveys are in the report appendix A (not read in detail).
